title: Tensor core utilization and power efficiency: A100 vs H100 vs L40S
content:
Purpose 
This note documents microbenchmark results focused on tensor-core utilization, SM occupancy, and power efficiency for three canonical GPUs we run in our serving fleet: NVIDIA A100 (40GB), H100 (80GB), and L40S (48GB). The goal: understand where inference throughput gains come from (tensor cores vs memory/PCIe), how power draw scales with batch size and sequence length, and produce a heuristic performance-per-watt figure we can use when recommending model-device pairings in Redwood Dedicated and Private.

Summary / TL;DR
- H100 shows the highest sustained tensor-core utilization on FP16/TF32 fused kernels for transformer attention and FFN blocks: ~65–80% depending on kernel mix. A100 is decent (45–60%), L40S trails on our fused kernels (30–50%) but is strong on memory-heavy ops.
- Power efficiency (throughput/W) favors H100 for large-batch high-util scenarios; for low-latency single-request traffic the L40S often yields better energy per inference because the H100 idles at higher base power.
- NVLink/PCIe topology matters: multi-GPU throughput per watt degrades when traffic crosses PCIe (p4d-like topologies) vs NVLink meshes (puh- and DGX-like).

Test matrix and methodology
- Kernels/workloads: scaled-down transformer encoder layers (1–24 layers) and a synthetic attention+FFN benchmark that exercises matmul+GELU+layernorm paths. We also ran a full small-LM inference (6.7B) with token-by-token generation to capture KV cache behavior.
- CUDA and driver matrix: CUDA 12.2 with driver 535.xxx on H100, CUDA 11.8 with 520.xxx on A100, CUDA 12.1 with 525.xxx on L40S. We explicitly profiled across two CUDA versions for a subset to confirm kernel changes.
- Measurement tools: Nsight Systems (end-to-end traces), Nsight Compute (kernel-level metrics), NVIDIA DCGM for SM/TX/Memory utilization, and nvidia-smi sampling for power (10 Hz). We also used our runtime's instrumented hooks to record per-request token latency and per-token FLOP counter estimates.
- Metrics reported: sustained TFLOPS (measured via matmul kernel counters), tensor-core utilization (% of eligible FP16/TF32 matmuls that used WMMA/TF32 Tensor cores), average power (W), energy per token (mJ/token), and SM occupancy (%).

Key results (high level)
- H100: sustained tensor TFLOPS in our fused attention+FFN bench peaked at ~78% of theoretical for large batches; average power at peak throughput ~420 W; energy per token ~1.9 mJ/token for 1k-token batch workloads.
- A100: sustained TFLOPS ~55% of theoretical under same kernels; average power ~300 W; energy per token ~2.6 mJ/token.
- L40S: sustained TFLOPS ~42% on fused kernels but memory throughput higher; average power ~260 W; energy per token ~2.1 mJ/token on small-batch, and ~1.8 mJ/token at medium batch sizes where memory-bound behavior amortizes.

Observed bottlenecks and behavior details
- Kernel fusion and layout: our runtime's fused GEMM+Bias+GELU kernels are critical to reach high tensor-core utilization. On H100, newer cuBLAS/cuDNN/TVM kernels automatically utilized TF32 acceleration, boosting effective tensor-use; on A100 older kernels needed explicit fusion to reach similar utilization. L40S required a layout change (NHWC-like packing) to avoid memory stalls in matmul.
- KV cache and memory bandwidth: for long seq (>= 2048) the limiting factor across all GPUs was memory bandwidth for KV reads/writes, not tensor core throughput. In these regimes A100 and L40S sometimes outperform H100 on energy per token because H100 spends more energy handling larger on-GPU caches and has higher base power.
- Low-latency (batch=1) mode: H100's high idle power (~175–200 W board power) penalizes energy per small request. L40S and A100 had lower idle power and produced lower mJ/token for batch=1 even with lower peak TFLOPS.

Topology and cloud SKU notes
- Cloud SKUs with NVLink (or backbone fabrics) preserved multi-GPU TFLOPS scaling and therefore better throughput/W for model parallel and sharded KV workloads. SKUs that expose GPUs over PCIe only (dense host configs) showed poor inter-GPU scaling leading to increased synchronization stalls and higher energy per token.
- Some cloud drivers on earlier stacks exposed conservative BFLOAT2/TF32 fallbacks that prevented tensor cores from being used in fused kernels; verify driver/CUDA compatibility when onboarding a region/instance type.

Actionable recommendations for product/operator teams
- For sustained high-throughput batch inference (throughput-first), prefer H100-backed dedicated pools: best throughput/W when batch sizes >= 16 and seq <= 1024.
- For latency-sensitive small-batch traffic, evaluate L40S or A100-backed pools—the lower idle power often yields better cost-efficiency for unpredictable traffic.
- Add a preflight device-capability probe in Private deployments that checks: tensor-core availability for our fused kernels, NVLink presence, driver/CUDA version, and memory bandwidth microbenchmark. Use that to auto-suggest quantization/tiling profiles.
- Document in Console an explicit "energy per token" estimate per model/pool derived from these benchmarks to help customers pick device types for Dedicated.

Open questions and next experiments
- Run the same matrix with FP8 optimized kernels (when available) to gauge whether L40S or A100 benefit more from lower-precision paths.
- Repeat KV-cache-dominant long-sequence experiments but with PCIe topology emulation to quantify cross-host penalties for KV sharding.
- Add thermal-throttling sweeps to check sustained throughput degradation over 24+ hour windows in different cloud SKUs.

Appendix: selected raw numbers (representative averages)
- Fused bench, batch=32, seq=512:
  - H100: tensor-util 72%, TFLOPS 210, power 420 W, mJ/token 1.95
  - A100: tensor-util 52%, TFLOPS 135, power 300 W, mJ/token 2.55
  - L40S: tensor-util 44%, TFLOPS 110, power 260 W, mJ/token 2.10
- KV-heavy, batch=8, seq=2048:
  - H100: tensor-util 38%, memory-bandwidth 820 GB/s, power 390 W, mJ/token 3.6
  - A100: tensor-util 30%, memory-bandwidth 780 GB/s, power 320 W, mJ/token 3.4
  - L40S: tensor-util 28%, memory-bandwidth 870 GB/s, power 310 W, mJ/token 3.1

Notes on reproducibility
- Benchmarks and scripts are in repo git:repo/benchmarks/power-profiles. Use the provided docker images which pin CUDA and driver helper utilities. Sampling rates and run length (warmup 120s, measure 300s) were chosen to reduce noise from frequency governors.

Concluding note
This document is an exploratory draft; results vary by kernel set and driver versions. The high-level signal is stable: H100 dominates at scale for tensor-heavy workloads, but A100/L40S remain competitive for latency-sensitive or memory-bound regimes and sometimes provide better energy per inference depending on workload shape. Next: formalize these findings into an internal "device selector" heuristic for Redwood Console and add an automated preflight test for Private deployments.
